Abstract: The effect of nanoparticles on the boiling heat transfer of refrigerant mixtures is studied. The mixtures are composed of refrigerant 134a and a polyolester lubricating oil.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of nanoparticle concentration on the pool boiling heat transfer performance of refrigerant/Al 2O3 nanolubrciant mixture on a reentrant boiling surface.
the effect of nanoparticle concentration on the boiling performance of nanolubricated refrigerant mixtures.
the effect of nanoparticle volume fraction on the pool boiling heat transfer coefficient of R134a in a nanolubricating mixture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nanolubrciants can improve the heat transfer performance of refrigerants, but only under specific conditions.

the addition of nanoparticles to R134a/polar lubricant mixtures can be used to enhance pool boiling on a reentrantly cavitated surface as long as: 1) The nanoparticles do not agglomerate, and 2) The nanoparticle concentration is sufficiently high.

the addition of nanoparticles in the base polyester lubricant can improve R134A pool boiling performance as long as the nanoparticle mass is sufficiently small and the nanoparticle size is sufficiently large.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

nanolubrification is a promising technique for improving R134a pool boiling performance on a reentrant boiling surface, as long as the nanolubrication concentration is sufficiently low to prevent nanoparticle agglomeration.

the addition of nanolubrication can enhance boiling performance of refrigerant mixtures, but only if the nanoparticles are dispersed in the lubrication and the nanoparticle mass concentration is sufficiently low.
nanolubrants can enhance R134a boiling heat transfer on reentrant cavity surfaces as long as the nanoparticle mass concentration is sufficiently small and the nanoparticles remain dispersed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nanoparticle mass fractions and the nanoparticle sizes must be carefully selected for the best performance.
nanoparticle mass fraction should be carefully controlled and that a minimum nanoparticle concentration is required to achieve an enhancement in the heat transfer.

nanoparticle agglomeration is a critical parameter in the design of nanolubricating fluids for refrigerant mixtures, and it is essential that nanoparticle concentration be optimized to avoid agglomeration and maximize heat transfer.
